A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and all 19 pages, including Appendices A-F. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical content apart from the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original Hawkes-process simulations, estimation errors and CPU timings in Section 4, with kernel reconstructions and additional scalability and sensitivity experiments in Appendices A and F.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation results in Section 4 and Appendices A and F, including estimation errors, CPU timings and reconstructed triggering kernels.

M1.justification: The penalized least-squares estimator, equivalent-kernel construction, unit dual coefficients and random Fourier feature implementation in Section 2 are identical.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same synthetic mutually-exciting and refractory scenarios, including the larger-data and 15-dimensional settings in Appendix F. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Exp, Gau, Ber and Bonnet remain the comparators in Tables 1-2 and F4; Table F3 retains the comparison between Bonnet and Ours. Comparator participation is unchanged.

E3.justification: The chronological 80/20 split, hyperparameter grids, integrated squared error and CPU-time metrics, model configurations and Appendix F experimental settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the kernel-reconstruction examples in Appendix A and the data-size scalability, dimensionality scalability and hyperparameter-grid sensitivity analyses in Appendix F.

E5.justification: Both report the same 10-trial main experiments, standard errors and Mann-Whitney U significance reporting. Appendix F's trial counts and uncertainty reporting also remain identical.

E6.justification: All results in Tables 1-2 and F3-F4 and the curves in Figures A1-A2 match. Appendix F.3 also retains the grid-refinement result of 0.58 ± 0.12 versus 0.59 ± 0.13.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, Propositions 2-4, their assumptions and derivations, the complexity analysis and the proofs in Appendices B-E are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about the representer theorem, analytically fixed dual coefficients and computational efficiency with competitive estimation accuracy.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of accuracy differences and scalability, along with the limitations concerning potentially negative intensities and cubic scaling with process dimensionality.

D1.justification: Feature counts, hyperparameters, baseline implementation sources, TensorFlow version, Apple M2 Max hardware and disabled-GPU setting are unchanged. No implementation or resource-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The citations, reference list and positioning relative to earlier representer theorems and Hawkes-process estimators are identical, including the distinction from Bonnet and Sangnier's approximation-based formulation.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 10 October 2025 to v2 dated 5 February 2026. This is a minor administrative text edit; the manuscript prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures A1-A2, Tables 1-2 and F3-F4, captions, axes and placement are identical. The manuscript layout is unchanged; the only visible difference is the version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, proofs, limitations and presentation are identical across both PDFs, including their appendices. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
